summary: In 1930-1932 Union Carbide and contractor Rinehart & Dennis drove the Hawks Nest Tunnel through near-pure silica rock in West Virginia without wet drilling or respirators, killing hundreds of mostly Black migrant workers from silicosis and covering it up.

evidence.note: groundbreaking on the tunnel at the end of March 1930
tunnel finished in 1932, well ahead of the two-year target
1936 House inquiry condemns the companies; respirator law follows
segregated shacks, scrip pay and lower wages for Black workers
company doctors misdiagnose silicosis and hand out sugar-pill placebos
armed rouster deputized by the county sheriff beats sick workers; fines from staged raids
modern black lung and silica exposure failures among US coal miners
segment on Rukeyser, her 1936 trip to Gauley Bridge and FBI surveillance

notes: Primary subject is the event, so roles are empty. Opening history of silicosis and Union Carbide's 1911-1919 dam origins are background and kept out of covered_span. The 2018 NPR/Frontline segment on today's black lung epidemic is a modern parallel rather than this disaster's direct legacy, so reaches_present is false; a reviewer could argue otherwise. Death toll estimates range from 464 to about 2,000.
